meta.name: Aditya Shah
meta.title: Technical Leadership · Cloud Infrastructure · Applied AI
meta.tagline: I lead technical teams, solve production problems, and build useful automation.

hero.description: Hosting Support Manager / DevOps Engineer at WPMU DEV. I lead distributed support engineers and stay hands-on with infrastructure, incidents, security, and automation.

whatIDo.title: Lead technical teams. Own the difficult conversations.
whatIDo.description: Lead distributed hosting support engineers, mentor the team, review quality, and own complex customer escalations. Turn recurring issues into clearer processes and better documentation.

whatIDo.title: Find the cause behind a production problem.
whatIDo.description: Investigate issues across Linux, Nginx, PHP-FPM, MySQL/MariaDB, DNS, and caching. Connect logs and observability with the customer’s experience, then coordinate the next steps.

whatIDo.title: Build AI workflows with useful, checkable outputs.
whatIDo.description: Use LLM APIs, structured outputs, and tool integrations for practical investigation and automation. Keep the reasoning visible and human judgment part of the workflow.

whatIDo.title: Make WordPress more reliable and secure.
whatIDo.description: Debug performance, multisite, WooCommerce, migrations, and plugin conflicts. Investigate compromised sites, support recovery, and address the conditions that let problems return.

whatIDo.title: Turn repeated work into reusable tools.
whatIDo.description: Build Bash scripts, Ansible workflows, and internal tools around real operational tasks. Document the decisions so the next engineer has a better starting point.

highlights: Lead a distributed hosting support team, with responsibility for hiring, mentoring, quality, SOPs, and knowledge systems.
Own critical customer escalations and coordinate production incident response across teams.
Debug Linux, Nginx, PHP, MySQL/MariaDB, WordPress, DNS, and caching issues; investigate compromised sites and support remediation.
Build automation and internal tooling with Ansible, Bash, REST APIs, and AI-assisted workflows.
experience.note: Company tenure since February 2019; current title shown, without implying it was held throughout.

highlights: Supported WooCommerce customers through plugin conflicts, PHP errors, and configuration issues; worked with developers on bug reports.
Built and maintained WordPress websites, configured hosting, and resolved plugin, PHP, and performance issues for clients.

community.description: Started with a meetup at my home in Bhopal. Over the years, it grew into 100+ meetups and community events connecting students, developers, site owners, and new contributors.
Speaker and organizer across WordCamps, including WordCamp Bhopal 2025 and the WordCamp Asia 2026 operations team.
Hands-on workshops introducing students to WordPress and open source.
Organize DevFest, Cloud Community Day, and hands-on AI workshops in Bhopal, helping people learn together and turn ideas into working projects.

summary: I lead Hosting Support at WPMU DEV and stay hands-on with the production problems behind customer escalations. My work connects distributed team leadership, Linux and WordPress infrastructure, security investigations, automation, and clear technical communication. I also build and write about practical AI workflows, with a focus on structured outputs and human review.
contributions: WP-CLI: open-source contributor to the WordPress command-line tool
WordPress.org: active community member and speaker
GitHub: public engineering work and tooling at github.com/ethicaladitya
